questions.question: In which of the following places is the Tomb of Ahmad Shah Al Wali Bahmani built?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ashtoor.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tomb of Ahmad Shah Al Wali Bahmani was built between 1436 and 1458,in Bidar, Karnataka.**
 
• Historical records indicate construction began upon his death in 1436.
 
• His son, **Allauddin Ahmad Shah II, commissioned the tomb** and had it completed sometime within his reign ending in 1458.

 
• The Bahamani kings were fond of building magnificent tombs to house themselves after death.
 
• The tombs of Ahamad Shah and Alauddin Shah II stand out due to their grandeur.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Major tombs in Ashtoor**

 
 
• **Tomb of Ahmad Shah Al Wali Bahamani**: Ahmad Shah Al Wali Bahamani’s tomb is built in square layout in a vast lofty building with thick walls. 
 
• **Tomb of Ahmad Shah’s Queen**: Has floral designs, religious texts and ceilings decorated with paintings.
 
• **Tomb of Sultan Allauddin Shah II**: Has lots of tile work as well as blue, green and yellow paintwork. Three tall entrance arches and a square hall are key features of this tomb.
 
• **Tomb of Sultan Humayun**: Built with black trap masonry, Humayun’s tomb is super thick but split open due to a lighting strike.
 
• **Tomb of Malika-i-Jahan:** Mallika was the wife of Sultan Humayun Shah. Her tomb has entrance arches elegantly decorated with stucco work.
 
• **Chaukhandi of Hazrat Khalil Ullah**: Saint Khalil-Ullah was the preceptor of princes Ahmad Shah and Allauddin. His tomb is a two storied building erected on a high platform.
 
• **Other tombs**: Tombs of Sultan Nizam Shah, Sultan Muhammad Shah III, Muhammad Shah Bahamani, Sultan Wali-Ullah and Sultan Kalim Ullah

questions.question: In the Winter Session of Parliament, which was held from 29 November 2021 to 22 December 2021, ___________ bills were passed (excluding an Appropriation Bill).
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**10**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **Winter Session of Parliament 2021**, which took place from **November 29, 2021, to December 22, 2021**, a total of **10 bills** were passed by both Houses of Parliament.
 
• The Bills Cover- Farm Law Repeal Bill, Assisted Reproductive Technology Regulation Bil, High Courts and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment Bill, Dam Safety Bill, 2019, Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __**Session Of Parliament:**__

 
• 
 
__**Budget Session (February to May)**__:

 __
 
• The **Budget Session** is considered highly crucial. It usually runs from February to May each year.
 
• During this session, the **Union Budget** is presented by the Finance Minister. Members of both Houses discuss various provisions of the budget and matters related to taxation.
 
• The session is generally split into two periods with a gap of one month between them. It commences with the President’s Address to both Houses.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Monsoon Session (July to September)**__:

 __
 
• The **Monsoon Session** follows a break of two months after the Budget Session.
 
• In this session, matters of public interest are discussed. It covers a wide range of topics relevant to governance and legislation.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Winter Session (November to December)__:**

 
 
• The **Winter Session** is the shortest of all sessions.
 
• It takes place from mid-November to mid-December.
 
• During this session, matters that could not be addressed earlier are taken up, compensating for any legislative business missed during the second session of the Parliament.

questions.question: Which is a saltwater lake located in the Tibet Autonomous Region, China, to the west of Lake Mansarovar and to the south of Mount Kailash?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Lake Rakshastal.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points

__
 
• **Lake Rakshastal is a saltwater lake **in Tibet Autonomous Region, China.

 
 
• Located to the west of** Lake Mansarovar and south of Mount Kailash.**** **
 
 
 
• According to Hindu mythology, **Ravana**, the demon-like King of Lanka, performed severe penance here to please **Lord Shiva**.
 
 
• The lake is also known as **Ravan Tal**.
 
 
 
• A short river named **Ganga Chhu** connects Lake Mansarovar with Rakshastal.
 
• Rakshastal covers an area of **250 square kilometers**.
 
 
• Its surroundings include **white cobbles**, hills, and a **dark red island**.
 
 
 
• Lake Rakshastal remains an integral part of the **Kailash-Manasarovar pilgrimage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lake Yamdrok Tso**__

 __
 
• **​**__Yamdrok Lake, also known as **Yamdrok Yumtso**, is sacred in Tibetan tradition.
 
• The lake lies to the **west of Lake Mansarovar** and to the **south of Mount Kailash**.
 
• It is one of the **three largest lakes in Tibet**, stretching over **72 km (45 mi)**. 
 __
 
• ​The lake is fan-shaped, spreading southward and narrowing to the north.
 
 
 
• Yamdrok Lake is surrounded by **snow-capped mountains** and fed by numerous small streams.
 
 
 
• **Lake Rawok**__ ​
 __
 
• Lake Rawok Tso, also known as **Rawok Lake**, is the **largest lake in eastern Tibet**.
 
• It is located in **Pasho County** within the **Chamdo prefecture**.
 
• Lake Rawok sits at an **altitude of 3,800 meters**.
 
• Surrounded by magnificent snow-capped mountains and lush forests, Rawok Lake offers breathtaking views.
 
 
 
• **Lake Basum Tso**__
 
 
• Lake Basum Tso, also known as **Basumtso Lake, is the lake in eastern Tibet.​**
 
• The lake is **surrounded by snow-capped peaks** and **natural forests**.
 
• It is not only a visual delight but also a **holy lake** for the **Nyingma sect** of Tibetan Buddhism

questions.question: In which of the following sports is the term ‘Leg bye’ used?
questions.solution:
correct answer is__** Cricket.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The term "**Leg bye" i**s used in the **sport of cricket.**
 
• In cricket, a leg bye is a** way for the batting team to score runs without the ball hitting the bat.**
 
• It occurs when the** ball makes contact with the batsman's body, **usually the leg, and then the batsmen run and score runs as a result of that contact.
 
• Leg byes are considered a form of extras, and the runs are added to the team's total.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• term used in football:
 
 
• **Kick,** **Goal, Head, Penalty kick, Dribble, **Offside, Move, Hattrick, Foul, Left out, Right out, Stopper, Defender, Side back.

questions.question: The Sun Temple of Modhera was built by the king of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solanki.**____** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points**__

__
 
• **The Sun Temple of Modhera **was **built by the Solanki Dynasty.**
 
• It was **constructed** during the reign of **Bhima I of the ****Chaulukya dynasty**(Also Called Solanki Dynasty) in the 11th century.​
 
 
• It was constructed around **1026-1027 CE**.
 
 
 
• This magnificent Hindu temple is **dedicated to** the solar deity **Surya.**
 
 
• ​Stands proudly in the village of Modhera, **located in the Mehsana district of Gujarat, India**.
 
 
 
• 
 
The **temple is situated** on the bank of the **river Pushpavat****i.**

 
 
• 
 
It was included in the tentative list of **UNESCO World Heritage Sites** in 2022.

 

 [IMAGE: https://www.gujarattourism.com/content/dam/gujrattourism/images/heritage-sites/sun-temple/gallery/Sun%20Temple19.jpg]

__
 
• **Rashtrakuta Dynasty**__

 __
 
• ​__The Rashtrakuta dynasty **ruled** large parts of **southern, central, and northern India** Between the** ****6th and 13th centuries.**
 
• They** came from India and settled in Manyakheta,** now Gulbarga in Karnataka.
 
• Rashtrakutas had a **power struggle with Pala and Prathihara** dynasties for control over the Gangetic plains.
 
• They made **significant contributions to ****mathematics, literature, and architecture****.** 
 __
 
• Their influence extended from the Ganges River to Kanyakumari.
 
 
 
• A notable Rashtrakuta king, **he authored the ****Kavirajamarga**, a significant literary work in Kannada.
 
 
 
• **Paramara Dynasty**__
 __
 
• **​**__The Paramaras ruled a region in India from around the **9th to 14th centuries.**
 
• Their main area was **Malwa**, which is in **central India**.
 
• One of their kings, **Bhoja**, was super famous. 
 __
 
• ​His empire stretched from **north to south** and **west to east**.
 
 
 
• The Paramaras faced challenges from other kingdoms and they moved their capital from one place to another.
 
 
 
• **Tomar Dynasty**__
 __
 
• **​**__The Tomaras were a group of **Rajput rulers** who ruled around **Delhi and Haryana**.
 
• They built a strong wall called **Lal Kot** around modern Delhi.
 
• Over time, they were replaced by other dynasties like the **Chahamanas** and **Ghurids**.

questions.question: ‘Moksha’ is an item of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Moksha"** symbolizes spiritual liberation in **Hindi Tradition**.
 
• A distinctive part of the Odissi tradition is the inclusion of Moksha (or Mokshya) finale in the performance sequence. 
 
• This the concluding item of a recital. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya**

 
 
• **Classical dance **form of **Assam**.
 
• Originated in **Vaishnavite monasteries **(Sattras).
 
• Rooted in devotional worship of **Lord Krishna and Radha**.
 
• Revived in the **20th century **and recognized as a **classical dance form in 2000**.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**
 
 
• Major classical dance form of India.
 
• Originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
 
• Combines nritta, nritya, and natya elements.
 
• 
 
Experienced a revival in the 20th century.

 
 
 
 
• **Kathak**
 
 
• **Classical dance **form of **North India**.
 
• Originated in **ancient temples**, **emphasizing storytelling**.
 
• Combines **rhythmic footwork, hand gestures, spins, and storytelling**.
 
• Known for various **gharanas **(schools) with **distinct styles**.
 
• Repertoire includes **themes **from **mythology, love, and history**.
 
• Emphasizes **technical precision **and **emotional expression**.

questions.question: Easter is celebrated on which of the following days of the week?
questions.solution:
correct answer is__** Sunday**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Easter Sunday is a **religious Christian holiday** that is observed globally to** celebrate the resurrection of Jesus Christ** .
 
• while **holidays like Christmas have fixed dates**, the date for Easter changes from year to year.
 
• According to the Bible, i**t marks the third day after Jesus was crucified **when he rose from the dead.
 
• Easter's exact date varies so much because it **actually depends on the moon**.
 
• The holiday is set to coincide with the **first Sunday after the Paschal Full Moon, the first full moon after the vernal equinox**.
 
• Around the world, Easter is celebrated in various ways, with many cultures incorporating their own traditions and customs into the holiday.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Christmas, Good Friday, and Easter a**re the t**hree major Christian festivals **observed in India.
 
• **Christmas is the most important** of these three celebrations for Christians.

questions.question: The East West Corridor connects ______ in India.
questions.solution:
correct answer is __**Silchar to Porbandar.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The East-West Corridor **connects Porbandar, Gujarat, in the west with Silchar, Assam, in the east.**
 
• Major cities in **Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam **are included in its coverage.
 
• Through NH 27, it travels a distance of **3,300 kilometres.**
 
• he East-West corridor of the Golden Quadrilateral connects Silchar and Porbandar cities in India.
 
• The **North-South–East-West Corridor is the largest highway project(ongoing) in India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) is the **largest express highway project in India**.

 
 
• It connects India's **four largest metropolises: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, and Chennai,** and thus, forms a quadrilateral of sorts.
 
• Bengaluru, Pune, Ahmedabad, and Surat are also served by this network.
 
• It is the largest highway project in India and the **fifth-longest in the world with 5846 kilometers**.
 
• Therefore, **Kolkata-Chennai is the longest corridor in the Golden Quadrilateral.**
